technical_and_design_decisions: Refactor the existing ModuleRegistry to use a dynamic, thread-safe in-memory registry (ConcurrentHashMap) to support runtime registration and deregistration of modules, eliminating the hardcoded bootstrap-time population via ModuleRegistryPopulator.

Implement the custom module upload REST API as a POST /dataflow/modules endpoint that accepts multipart JAR uploads, with role-based access control aligned with existing Spring Cloud Data Flow security configurations.
Integrate module upload functionality into the Spring Cloud Data Flow Shell as a first-class 'module upload' command that mirrors the REST API functionality for CLI users.

Migrate all Spring XD modules to the spring-cloud-stream-modules (s-c-s-m) repository, update their baseline to Spring Boot 3.x, Java 17, and Spring Cloud Stream 4.x to align with Spring Framework 6.0 requirements specified in the specification.
Reuse existing Spring Cloud Data Flow module metadata validation and schema checking logic for uploaded custom modules to ensure consistency with pre-packaged module requirements.
Migrated modules will be tagged with a version suffix (e.g., -scs) to distinguish them from legacy Spring XD modules and avoid version conflicts.
assumptions: The 's-c-s' repository reference in user stories U6-U8 is a typographical error and intended to be 's-c-s-m' (spring-cloud-stream-modules repository) to align with U3-U5, as all user stories describe moving modules to a repository for use as streaming pipeline sources.
Publicly available source code for all referenced Spring XD modules (jms, mail, mongo, mqtt, reactor-ip, stdout) is accessible and can be migrated without licensing restrictions.

Existing Spring Cloud Data Flow infrastructure for REST API scaffolding, security, shell command framework, and module metadata handling is available for reuse, eliminating the need to build these components from scratch.
No changes to existing stream/task creation workflows are required beyond making migrated and custom uploaded modules available in the module registry.
All migrated modules will be compatible with existing Spring Cloud Stream binders (e.g., Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ) without additional binder-specific modifications.
